description: Ordered, deterministic rule set for EU AI Act risk tiering. The engine evaluates rules top-to-bottom; the FIRST rule whose conditions all match assigns the tier and halts. If none match, the default tier applies. Precedence: PROHIBITED > HIGH > LIMITED > MINIMAL.

default.rationale: No prohibited practice, Annex III / Annex I high-risk trigger, or transparency trigger was identified. The system is treated as minimal-risk; voluntary codes of conduct are encouraged.

rules.rationale: Performs social scoring of natural persons leading to detrimental or unjustified treatment — a prohibited practice.
Real-time remote biometric identification in publicly accessible spaces for law enforcement — a prohibited practice (subject to narrow statutory exemptions not assessed here).
Infers emotions of individuals in workplace or education settings — a prohibited practice (outside medical/safety exceptions).
Biometric categorisation inferring sensitive attributes — a prohibited practice.
Predicts criminal offending based solely on profiling or personality traits — a prohibited practice.
Builds or expands facial-recognition databases via untargeted scraping — a prohibited practice.
The AI is a safety component of, or is itself, a product covered by Annex I harmonisation law requiring third-party conformity assessment — high-risk under Art. 6(1).
Intended purpose falls within an Annex III high-risk category and no Art. 6(3) derogation applies — high-risk.

rules.note: Annex III category selected but Art. 6(3) derogation asserted — not high-risk on that basis. Evaluation continues to transparency and minimal tiers. The derogation assertion must be documented and, where required, registered.
rules.rationale: Art. 6(3) derogation asserted for an Annex III system.
Directly interacts with natural persons — subject to transparency obligations (inform users they are interacting with an AI).
Generates or manipulates synthetic content — subject to transparency/marking obligations.
